brief: RBC stays on the sidelines with Tech (market weight, downgraded from overweight Oct 14) and keeps Health Care overweight: since the swap Health Care has been the top S&P 500 sector and Tech the second-worst. The downgrade rested on expensive median P/E, weaker flows, decelerating Semis EPS revisions, an overdue 5-10% tier-1 pullback, and a looming geographical rotation; none of that has reversed enough to get off the sidelines, though Tech valuations have modestly improved. RBC holds its 12-month S&P 500 target at 8,150 and still expects a tier-1 pullback given Iran-war risk, possible 2027 EPS cuts, the midterms, and new Fed hikes. On the midterms, a Cook Political Report shift toward a Democratic Senate edge moved RBC's split-Congress read from neutral-to-modestly-positive to neutral-to-positive; RBC rates a Democratic sweep neutral-to-negative and a Republican sweep positive, and is less bullish than consensus on a post-midterm rally, noting stocks historically only rally hard afterward if the S&P 500 fell in 3Q or 4Q of the election year. Separately, RBC turns constructive on Small Caps over Large Caps given stable Fed-hike expectations, undemanding valuations, and closing short positioning, while flagging thin cyclical support as a risk to the call.
